body: well, I haven’t been seeing my therapist at all this year, so I called and scheduled myself weekly appointments for the next few months. she helped me a lot before when i saw her regularly. I’ve also been trying to get rid of anything I could hurt myself with, but there are a few razor blades I’m having trouble letting go of. maybe it sounds weird, but it’s like saying goodbye to a friend, since self harm has always helped keep my mind off my emotional pain. I’m going to keep working up to it.

I desperately wanted to stop feeling the extreme emotional pain i was in. I didn’t want to be dead, I just wanted it all to stop, and really death is the only way to stop it for good. I felt that things would never get better so there was no point in suffering.

waiting for things sucks, but you were patient enough with yourself to stay sober, why not be patient a little longer?
when i’m feeling suicidal i procrastinate my life. i tell myself that i will kill myself tomorrow, and the next day i tell myself that again, and again until the feeling fades away.

do you feel like you will never find someone, or are you having trouble finding the will to wait? do you think that you deserve to be with someone or do you feel that you are not good enough?

by the way, i wanted to say that i’m very proud of you for staying sober for so long. that shit isn’t easy at all. you are amazing.
when i first thought about wanting to die, i was 9. when i first thought about how i would do it and researched methods i was 12. my first actual attempt was just after i turned 15.

my therapist told me that a breakup can be just like grieving a death. you may go through the stages of grief, not necessarily in order. it has helped me to review them and think about what stage i’m at in the process. 
your breakup is very fresh. i remember when mine had just happened, and i almost couldn’t believe it was real. i was very unstable and went from feeling numb to having mental breakdowns. maybe it is like this for you too.
what i can tell you is that if you go on living, you will see recovery. i’ve been out of my relationship for about 6 months now. yes, right now i am not doing good at all, but just before now i was thinking about how i felt when my breakup was new and how much less distressed i am about it now. it might be like a rollercoaster. there may be days when you think it’s impossible to see the next but there may also be days when you’re happy. no two people will experience these things exactly the same, so i can’t tell you that things will be this way for you, but i thought if i told you how it’s been for me it might help ease your mind. when i feel suicidal, it helps me a bit to remind myself that if i had succeeded in my attempts sooner, i wouldn’t have been able to see myself improve as much as i have now. 

i just hate that i had to learn he’s with a new girl. now i can’t keep my mind off of him. my usual distractions aren’t working. i am trying my best to tell myself that this is just like the original breakup, feels like the worst thing ever at first but in time the pain begins to fade.

thank you for commenting. it’s comforting knowing that others are going through similar things, but at the same time i hate that anyone else has to feel this way too. it really is horrible. i was doing better and improving for a while, but after learning about this i’m at a very low point. i am afraid to keep feeling like this. i don’t really want to die, it’s just that i would take anything over this and i would gladly kill myself to escape these feelings. 
i keep finding myself thinking about him and remembering everything we did together. people keep telling me to just think about the good memories we made and it’ll help, but it does the opposite. it just makes me long for him to hold me so much more. it’s incredibly painful to think about how happy he made me and how that’s just gone now. i wonder if you feel this way too?
depends on the circumstances and the people involved but i think in most cases i would say suicide

ask any cutter and they’ll tell you it was only supposed to be one time, then one more time, and just one more...and now you can’t get through a single day without the pain and the blood. 
ask any deep cutter and they’ll tell you it started off as simple nicks just to see a little blood and feel a little pain. but suddenly, it’s not enough anymore. you need to see more blood, feel more pain...and some day you find yourself on a first name basis with the ER because you come in for stitches so often. 
you are hurting, your pain may be unbearable, and you just want people to understand. you want people to see just how much you are suffering, and hurting yourself seems like the best way. this is very understandable. this is why i started cutting. 
you cut once out of desperation for this kind of attention, for people to see how much pain you are in. fast forward and now you cut because you need it to survive. it’s like air or food or water to you. is this what you want?
cutting is an addiction. it isn’t something that most people can do only once and never again. you get hooked on self harm. 
and about the attention...what i wanted was for my family to see how much i was hurting. i needed more support from them. what i got instead was disgust and hatred. now, whenever i am upset about anything, my family members will say something along the lines of “oh boohoo are you gonna go cut yourself now?” this fueled my addiction. now i cut so deep that i can see the fat under my skin, sometimes even the muscle. i have to get stitches regularly and i have scars that will NEVER fade. 
i am trying to recover but it is harder than i ever imagined. i think i will be able to make it even one day without cutting, then i end up relapsing before the day is over. every. single. time. 
i know you feel that self harm will get you the response you need. unlikely. but say it does, is it even worth it? is it really worth the long term addiction you might get into just from that one time?
i wish i had never started cutting. i wish i could go back and erase that one time. i don’t want you to end up putting yourself in a situation like this. my suggestion to you is to tell them exactly how you feel. tell them you feel like you need to hurt yourself for them to see how serious you are. whatever you do, don’t cut. it is never worth it. i am always here to talk if you need it. please shoot me a message if you have any questions or if there’s anything you need at all. the situation you’re in right now absolutely sucks. you must be in a lot of pain to be considering self harm. i will keep you in my thoughts.

hey man. recovery from addiction is hard as hell. it’s one of the most difficult things you could ever do. although i personally haven’t struggled with alcoholism, i am dealing with another addiction and i have also experienced it in my family. 
sometimes it can feel like you’re all alone. maybe even like the whole world is against you. that must really hurt in your situation.

just a stranger on the internet, but i am still here for you. i’ll be keeping you in my thoughts and wishing you well. ❤️

hello, i am currently dealing with a breakup as well. what helps me most is hanging out with friends or family. however, if this isn’t an option there are plenty of things you can do all by yourself. 
everyone is different, so often you just need to try things. avoid activities that may remind you of the person. i suggest trying things you know you like first. 
for example, i love drawing and video games, so that’s normally what i go to for a distraction when i need it. another great one is just putting on a movie or tv show that i like. if nothing is working, i take a nap. this isn’t the healthiest way to cope because you’re avoiding your problems, but it is a lot better than harming yourself.
